To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fracture properties along the ligament of a fracture specimen are size dependent and that the size dependence of the fracture properties can be explained by introducing a concept local fracture energy, which is size independent and can be determined from the fracture properties of the ligament.
the local fracture energies are non-uniform along the ligament, and that the boundary influence is the reason why the traditional fracture energy is size dependent.
the size effect on specific energy is due to a size-dependent influence of the boundary condition on the local fracture energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the boundary effect on fracture energy of concrete.
the effect of boundary conditions on the size-dependent fracture energy of concrete.
the fracture energy of concrete and its boundary effect on the fracture energy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the size effect on the fracture properties is a boundary effect and can be explained by the non-uniform distribution of fracture energy along the ligament.

the size effect of the fracture energy can be eliminated by introducing the concept of local fracture-energy,which is the energy dissipated in the fracture process zone per unit volume of the ligament.
, in general, the size of the specimen does affect the value of the fracture energy, and the effect is not necessarily linear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the local fracture energies along the ligament are not uniform,which leads to the size effect of traditional fracture energy,while the size independent local fracture energy can be determined by the proposed model.
the boundary influence is the main reason for the size dependence of the specific fracture energy in concrete,which should be considered for the fracture design of structures.
the fracture energy is a local property of material,not a property of the material itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the boundary effect is a major source of the size-dependence on fracture energy.
a size-independent fracture energy of concrete can be obtained by using the local fracture energy concept,which is a new idea to overcome the problem of specimen size effect.
the fracture process zone in a concrete specimen is not homogeneous and that the local fracture toughness is a non-uniform function of the distance from the specimen boundary.
